note: Round 9b, from the r8 panel's must-fix. This is what a teacher gets out of Excel or Google Sheets when her handout has a Lesson column: `Lesson | Chinese | English`. parse.ts gave the term slot to the FIRST Chinese column unconditionally, and round 7c's marker rule then promoted that marker to a glossed pair, so this paste returned five cards reading 第1课=apple, 第2课=banana and so on: every word she typed gone, and in its place a confident WRONG ANSWER KEY (the class plays a game whose answer to `apple` is `chapter 1`). Main was broken too but visibly so, two obvious junk cards she deletes; this was invisibly broken, which is worse for a teacher who will not proofread forty rows. The rule needs TWO Chinese columns to fire, so fixture 66 (`第1课\tLesson one`, one Chinese column) still keeps the marker as its term and her pair is still a card: round 7c is not reopened. Only a DOC-STRUCTURE marker is dropped this way (课, 单元, 章), never a countable one, because `第1天` can be the word she meant and the round 9 unit split exists to say so. THE RESIDUAL THIS NOTE USED TO RECORD IS CLOSED (round 11b, fixture 76): `第1周\t苹果\tapple` x3 answered 第1周=apple until the rule learned to ask per COLUMN.
